candidates.title: Compare supplier confirmations with purchase orders

demandEvidence.chore: Compare supplier confirmation line items with the original purchase order across SKU, quantity, price and delivery date.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: When a supplier confirmation contains dozens of line items, manually comparing every SKU, quantity, price, and delivery date against the original Purchase Order becomes time-consuming.

ease.reason: A beginner can test operator-entered sample rows, but no supplied implementation reference supports document extraction or matching.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: ecommerce operators handling supplier orders may pay to reduce manual comparisons; the post proves no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare two supplied tables and flag differences; varied documents and match accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A fixed comparison can flag rows repeatedly, but a person must supply records and verify each mismatch; mechanics lack reference support.

evidence.reason: The fresh post names the manual comparison and four fields, but gives no frequency, sample data or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a synthetic row-comparison experiment is scorable, but no supplied implementation reference supports the mechanics and prior assessments found no new evidence.
